# 2 Baruch Chapter 24 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 24 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 24:1 — "habitation / dwelling / world"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "this-habitation" | Syriac uses a dwelling/residence term for the current world |
| LOGOS | "this habitation" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "this world" | Simplifies for modern readers; but loses distinction from v.2 |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "this habitation" (EMET/LOGOS). The term must be distinguished from "the world" promised to the righteous in v.2 — using the same word for both would confuse the contrast.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS. Semantic distinction preserved.

---

## 24:1 — "storehouse of works / treasury of works"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-store-[house] of-works kept-in-the-treasury" | Two-stage: storehouse = location; treasury = God's keeping |
| LOGOS | "a storehouse of works kept in the treasury" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "their works are stored up and kept in your treasury" | Paraphrase, loses the storehouse imagery |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "a storehouse of works kept in the treasury." Both EMET and LOGOS distinguish the "storehouse" (the deposit) from the "treasury" (the divine keeping). PNEUMA conflates them.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 24:3 — "woe to us / how tragic"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "woe-is-it that-we-are-now [here]" | Preserves the Syriac woe-exclamation form |
| LOGOS | "woe to us that we are here now" | Formal retention of the lament |
| PNEUMA | "how tragic that we are here now" | Modernizes the exclamation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "woe to us." The Syriac lament form (wai lan) is a strong exclamation; "woe" preserves its rhetorical force. PNEUMA's "how tragic" is weaker.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Rhetorical register preserved.

---
